title: Scrooge's Christmas
text:
Ebenezer Scrooge was a hard, grasping old moneylender in London. On Christmas Eve he turned away his cheerful nephew Fred's invitation to dinner, refused gentlemen collecting for the poor, and grudged his clerk, Bob Cratchit, both an extra lump of coal and the day off. Christmas, he said, was humbug.

That night the ghost of his dead partner, Jacob Marley, appeared in chains forged by his own greed and warned that three spirits would visit him. The Ghost of Christmas Past showed Scrooge the lonely boy he had been, the happy apprentice at Fezziwig's dances, and the young woman who had left him because he loved money more. The Ghost of Christmas Present took him to the Cratchits' small, happy feast, where Tiny Tim, a crippled little boy, said, "God bless us, every one," and the spirit warned that the child would die if nothing changed. The Ghost of Christmas Yet to Come showed him a dead man whom nobody mourned, his belongings sold off by servants, the Cratchit home grieving for Tim, and finally a neglected gravestone with Scrooge's own name.

Scrooge woke on Christmas morning, alive and weeping with joy. He sent the biggest turkey in the shop to the Cratchits, gave generously to the poor, and went to dinner at Fred's. The next day he raised Bob's salary. He became a second father to Tiny Tim, who did not die, and as good a friend and master as the old city knew.
lesson: It is never too late to change how you treat the people around you. Generosity done today is worth more than regret later.
people: Ebenezer Scrooge, Bob Cratchit, Tiny Tim, Fred
